method: Pixel positions read from the object mask (chroma >= 22 within x 430..930, y 0..900) of the named file plus ruled crops of the same file. Normalised by the overall photographed height (866 px) unless a row says otherwise. PHOTOGRAPH-DERIVED PROPORTION, NOT A SURVEY: one studio viewpoint, residual perspective on the corner horns (their side faces are partly visible), no scale bar, no measured drawing.

pixel_readings.arch_motifs: alternating grape cluster / lily, grape at both ends (7 arches, so the pattern is symmetric)

proportions.feature: horn cap underside / fluted shaft top
proportions.note: two-step abacus above a fluted shaft

pierced zer base = top surface = cornice top
proportions.note: the 2-amot book height is taken TO HERE

32 teeth per face at 11.2 px pitch

book_vs_photograph: Book p. 255: 1 x 1 x 2 amot at the five-tefach amah = 41.667 x 41.667 x 83.333 cm. The photographed altar is base-to-top-surface / width = 2.182, i.e. about 9% slimmer than the book's 2.000. The BOOK wins: the modelled box is 41.667 wide and 83.333 high to the burning surface, so the model is slightly squatter than the photograph.

The pierced zer and the four horns stand ABOVE the burning surface in the photograph and are modelled that way, so the model is 83.333 + 7.79 cm tall overall. Reading the 2 amot to the horn tips instead would make the body 1.66:1, further from the photograph; that reading is not used.
Rings and poles: the Temple's golden altar has none (dossier section 3; the Institute's object has none). IncenseAltarV2 modelled poles; they are dropped here.

silhouette_overlap.method: Both silhouettes are reduced to binary masks, each stretched to its own bounding box on a common 200-column grid (the photograph fixes the grid aspect), then intersection over union. This scores SHAPE AND PROPORTION only. It is not a fidelity measure of ornament, and the photograph is a slightly oblique studio view, so a perfectly frontal model cannot reach 1.0.
silhouette_overlap.refinement_stopped_because: The altar reached 0.9525 at iteration 0 from the raw calibration; the two later iterations moved it by less than 0.001, so the raw calibration is kept unless a later iteration wins outright.
